## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Trump halts Russia sanctions package two days before deadline, citing national interest

On October 16, 2026, President Trump signed an executive order waiving sanctions and tariffs from the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026—legislation he himself had signed in September. The waiver covered duties of up to 100% on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil and gas. The move came just 48 hours before the sanctions were set to take effect and prompted immediate bipartisan criticism from lawmakers and Ukrainian officials.

**Why it matters.** Oil supply disruptions and geopolitical repositioning directly affect global commodity prices and inflation—the macro signals that matter for anyone running quant strategies or managing market risk. For India, this softens pressure on oil prices at a moment when crude imports remain critical to managing CAD and RBI's inflation mandate. More broadly, the decision signals Trump's warming toward Russia weeks before US midterms, which could reshape Great Power alignment and India's strategic calculus: if US-Russia tensions ease, Delhi's value as a Washington counterweight to Beijing weakens, pushing India toward deeper "Strategic Autonomy" and Europe-leaning partnerships.

**Action.** Monitor Brent crude's reaction and watch for any shift in India's oil sourcing patterns or official commentary on US-Russia détente. Track whether this signals a broader pattern of sanctions rollback under Trump, which would reorder energy markets and geopolitical leverage for the next 18 months.

### Iran accuses US of stoking Strait of Hormuz tensions as oil chokepoint risk rises

On October 19, 2026, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi blamed the United States for escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz during a joint press conference with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Araqchi called for regional issues to be resolved through diplomacy. The statement comes as Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and US-Iran military posturing have pushed oil prices toward $100 a barrel and threatened the world's most critical energy chokepoint, through which roughly one-third of seaborne oil passes.

**Why it matters.** The Strait of Hormuz is the arterial passage for global energy; any interruption cascades immediately into inflation, currency volatility, and central bank policy worldwide. For India, which imports roughly 80% of its oil and sources over half from the Middle East, this is not abstract geopolitics—it's a direct vector for import costs, rupee depreciation, and RBI rate decisions. An escalation here could force Delhi to diversify suppliers faster, court Russia or Central Asia more aggressively, and revise fiscal planning around energy subsidies.

**Action.** Watch spot Brent and oil futures volatility; cross-check latest Iranian and US military positioning in the Gulf via CENTCOM releases. Track India's energy ministry statements on supply resilience and any acceleration of non-Middle East sourcing—particularly from Russia, Central Asia, or Africa.

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 raises the floor on open coding and agent models

DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, a snapshot update to its September flash model that improves agentic and coding performance. Terminal-Bench 4.0 climbs to 42.3 from 31.2, Humanity's Last Exam (without tools) to 42.6 from 36.8, and DeepSWE v1.1 to 77.0 from 74.2. The weights ship on Hugging Face under MIT, and API pricing stays unchanged.

**Why it matters.** This is not a new model family but a meaningful calibration—the kind that moves the needle for practitioners running agent loops in production. Open weights at this capability level matter: engineers building multi-step reasoning chains or autonomous workflows now have a fully permissive baseline they can quantize, fine-tune, or deploy locally. The improvements in agent benchmarks (Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE) signal the model's optimization for tool use and code generation, not raw chat capability. Caveat: Anthropic's Opus 5 still leads on most shared benchmarks, so this is agentic parity for an open model, not dominance.

**Action.** If you are shipping agentic systems or code generation pipelines, run Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE v1.1 against both V4.1-Flash-1017 and your current baseline (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Luna) to find the best latency-accuracy trade-off for your task. The open weights make this model a candidate for local deployment in high-throughput agent scenarios. Read the paper on KV cache compression (arxiv 2609.19969) to understand the architecture.

### MiniMax M3.1 Flash prices agentic inference at $0.15/M input tokens

MiniMax shipped M3.1 Flash on October 19, a 428-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters. Input pricing is $0.15 per million tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, a 10× undercut to Opus 5.5 on input cost. It scores 76.2 on BankerToolBench and 82 on CyberGym, trades more than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on coding benchmarks but leads on task automation. Weights are promised October 23.

**Why it matters.** Cost per benchmark point is the new war, and MiniMax is pricing aggressively for agent workloads. At $0.15/M input, even high-token-count prompts (16K context, repeated samples for Monte Carlo reasoning) become economically viable at scale. The automation benchmark strength (BankerToolBench, CyberGym) hints that the model is optimized for workflows with tool calls and state transitions, not pure reasoning. Architectural question: does the MoE gating learn to route agent planning and tool use to the active set? If so, this becomes the default choice for cost-sensitive agentic inference.

**Action.** Benchmark M3.1 Flash's latency on your agent prompts (use 32K context to activate the full routing) and compare total cost-per-task against Claude Haiku 5.5 (more reasoning capability, higher cost) and DeepSeek Flash-1017 (open weights, no per-token billing). Read MiniMax's paper on MoE design to understand which 23B parameters activate for your task patterns.

## 🇮🇳 India

### Jio Platforms IPO Opens Today—India's Largest Public Offering Ever Anchored at ₹8,110 Crore

Jio Platforms' initial public offering opened on October 21, 2026, marking India's largest IPO to date. The company secured ₹8,110 crore (approximately $970 million) in anchor investor commitments from 212 institutional investors, including BlackRock and Fidelity, before retail trading began. The mainboard issue follows Reliance Industries' strategic separation of its digital and retail units into Jio Platforms, capitalizing on India's digital infrastructure momentum and investor appetite for large-cap tech plays.

**Why it matters.** For engineers and founders in India's AI and startup ecosystem, the Jio IPO signals institutional confidence in digital infrastructure and consumer tech at scale. The anchor demand shows that offshore capital still sees India as a growth market despite funding slowdowns elsewhere. This creates a ceiling raise for Series A/B startups in fintech, SaaS, and infrastructure layers—if a mega-cap digital play can command this kind of capital, tier-two startups have room to push valuations. The IPO also unlocks Reliance's balance sheet to invest in deeptech and AI, potentially competing with VC-backed founders for resources and talent.

**Action.** Monitor the IPO close-out on Oct 24 for retail subscription data and allotment numbers; they'll signal retail appetite for Indian tech. Read Reliance's offer document (RHP) on the NSE/BSE website to understand Jio's capex plans and AI/cloud expansion roadmap—it will inform where corporate capital is flowing.

### Even Healthcare Lands $50M Series B from Khosla Ventures, Signaling Heat in AI Healthcare

Even Healthcare, an AI-driven healthcare startup, raised $50 million in a Series B funding round led by Khosla Ventures on October 19, 2026. The capital will fund product expansion and market penetration across India's tier-2 and tier-3 cities where telehealth adoption is accelerating. The round arrives as healthtech AI companies tap strong institutional demand—competing directly with consumer fintech for the attention of overseas VCs and domestic impact investors backing digital health solutions.

**Why it matters.** Healthcare AI is one of three pillar sectors capturing deep-tech funding in India (alongside semiconductor and climate tech). Even's $50M raise at a time when general startup funding is moderating shows that healthcare AI with a clear path to profitability can still attract Tier-1 VCs. For engineers and founders considering healthtech roles or founding in the space, this validates the market thesis that India's fragmented healthcare system creates an unfair advantage for digitally-native AI-first players. The round also signals that Khosla's India thesis centers on AI-enabled services businesses, not just infrastructure.

**Action.** Check Even Healthcare's product positioning and unit economics (available in press releases); trace their fundraise history via Crunchbase to understand the typical Series A-to-B step for healthtech startups in India. Review Khosla's other Indian portfolio bets in healthcare and AI to identify co-investor patterns.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Tenstorrent Closes $1.5B Series E at $6.2B Valuation, Rejects Acquisition Offers from Intel and Qualcomm

Tenstorrent announced October 19, 2026, a $1.5 billion Series E financing round at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, more than tripling its earlier $2 billion valuation from December 2024. The round was led by Trace Capital and Innovation X, with support from existing backers ARK Invest, Fidelity, Morgan Stanley, SanDisk, T. Rowe Price, and Tether Investments. CEO Jim Keller told Bloomberg the company declined acquisition conversations with Intel and Qualcomm to instead raise venture capital and accelerate volume manufacturing and commercial expansion.

**Why it matters.** Tenstorrent's refusal to sell signals founder confidence in building an independent AI chip stack—a bet that custom silicon for enterprise inference is a durable standalone business, not a feature to be absorbed by larger players. The $6.2B valuation reflects investor conviction that non-Nvidia AI chip companies can command meaningful exit multiples if they reach customer scale. For founders in deeptech, the signal is clear: post-training infrastructure is attracting more capital than traditional semiconductor M&A, and this round proves there's an alternative path to acquisition.

**Action.** Track Tenstorrent's customer deployments (the company serves hyperscalers and enterprises). Founders building AI infrastructure should study how the company positioned itself as indispensable enough to decline acquisition—that's the playbook for raising at higher valuations in a consolidation-prone sector.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### FDA Approves Bepirovirsen, First Antisense Drug for Functional Cure in Chronic Hepatitis B

The FDA approved bepirovirsen (brand name Hibsago) on October 20, 2026, marking the first disease-modifying therapy to achieve functional cure in chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Phase 3 trials B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 enrolled 1,834 patients across 29 countries, who received weekly subcutaneous injections of 300 mg bepirovirsen or placebo for 24 weeks alongside ongoing nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. At week 72, functional cure—defined as sustained HBsAg clearance—reached 20% in B-Well 1 (127/650) and 19% in B-Well 2 (106/570), compared to 0% placebo; in patients with lower baseline HBsAg, functional cure rates climbed to 25% and 28% respectively.

**Why it matters.** Functional cure of chronic HBV has been a 30-year goal—this is the first finite-duration therapy (24 weeks of injections) to deliver it in a measurable fraction of patients without requiring lifetime suppressive therapy. For the 250 million people chronically infected, this alters the treatment paradigm from indefinite antivirals to a curative shot. The 23% rate of sustained HBV DNA suppression after therapy discontinuation suggests durable immune reconstitution, not temporary viral suppression. Bepirovirsen's mechanism—silencing HBsAg production via antisense oligonucleotide—is mechanistically novel and opens a first-in-class platform.

**Action.** Read the published trial (Hou JL et al., NEJM, May 28, 2026) and the full interim data at EASL 2026. For clinicians, this reshapes treatment sequencing in non-cirrhotic HBV: patients with low baseline HBsAg are the priority cohort. For investors, this validates the antisense-for-viral-disease thesis and may unlock similar programs in HCV, HBV variants, and other difficult-to-cure viruses. For patients: discuss with hepatologists whether you are a candidate (requires confirmed cirrhosis-free status, ongoing NA therapy).

*Sources: [hcplive.com](https://www.hcplive.com/view/fda-approves-bepirovirsen-for-chronic-hepatitis-b) · [ajmc.com](https://www.ajmc.com/view/bepirovirsen-achieves-clinically-meaningful-functional-cure-rates-in-chronic-hepatitis-b) · [hospitalhealthcare.com](https://hospitalhealthcare.com/specialisms/gastroenterology/bepirovirsen-delivers-functional-cure-for-chronic-hepatitis-b-virus-infections-phase-3-trials-show/)*

### Dostarlimab Achieves 47% Complete Response in Rectal Cancer Without Surgery or Chemotherapy

The FDA granted accelerated approval to dostarlimab on October 19, 2026, for mismatch-repair-deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite-instable (MSI-H) locally advanced rectal cancer. The phase 2 AZUR-1 trial enrolled 144 patients who received dostarlimab monotherapy every 3 weeks. At 12 months, independent central review confirmed sustained clinical complete response in 47% (95% CI 37–56%), with an objective response rate of 79% (CI 71–85%); at median follow-up of 26.3 months, none of the complete responders experienced disease progression. Importantly, 68% achieved clinical complete response by investigator assessment, allowing the majority to avoid neoadjuvant chemoradiation and surgery.

**Why it matters.** This reframes locally advanced rectal cancer for a molecular subset—dMMR/MSI-H tumors, which comprise 5–10% of cases. Avoiding chemoradiation and colectomy preserves sphincter function, fertility, and quality of life while maintaining or improving survival. The durability signal (zero progressions in responders at 26+ months) is robust for accelerated approval and suggests immune-induced durable control. This is an inflection point for checkpoint-inhibitor monotherapy in solid tumors previously managed by multimodal surgery and chemotherapy.

**Action.** Full AZUR-1 interim data will be presented at ESMO Congress 2026 (October 23–27); clinicians should review biomarker selection (dMMR/MSI-H testing is critical). For patients with newly diagnosed locally advanced rectal cancer, request molecular profiling before committing to neoadjuvant chemo-radiation. This approval is accelerated and contingent on a confirmatory trial, so ongoing surveillance for long-term relapse is warranted. Oncologists should consider dostarlimab a first-line option for eligible MSI-H cases.

*Sources: [ascopost.com](https://ascopost.com/news/october-2026/fda-approves-dostarlimab-for-msi-hdmmr-locally-advanced-rectal-cancer/) · [targetedonc.com](https://www.targetedonc.com/view/dostarlimab-demonstrates-sustained-complete-responses-in-dmmr-msi-h-rectal-cancer) · [gsk.com](https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/jemperli-dostarlimab-achieves-sustained-clinical-complete-responses-in-dmmrmsi-h-locally-advanced-rectal-cancer/)*

## 🎤 Culture & World

### Blondie Returns With Johnny Marr and First Album in 9 Years

Blondie dropped "Spectral Eyes" on October 15, the lead single from *High Noon*, their 12th studio album and first new material since 2017. The track features Johnny Marr (ex-Smiths guitarist) writing and performing guitar alongside bassist Glen Matlock and co-founding drummer Clem Burke. The album releases February 26, 2027, via BMG.

**Why it matters.** Nine years between albums is near-permanent silence in the streaming era—most bands don't survive that gap culturally. Blondie's return with Marr signals they're not chasing nostalgia but staking a claim on legacy credibility. For creators and tech audiences, this is a distribution play: a 1970s–80s new-wave band betting that legacy acts still command attention when paired with credible modern collaborators. Marr's involvement elevates this beyond reunion fare. The jangly, synth-driven "Spectral Eyes" reads as a deliberate statement that the playbook still works.

**Action.** Stream "Spectral Eyes" across platforms and watch for the full *High Noon* campaign launching into 2027. This is Clem Burke's final recording—the album functions as a career capstone for one of new wave's most iconic drummers.

### South Korea's Asian Games Gold Exposes Military Service Exemption Backlash

South Korea won its fourth consecutive men's football gold at the October 4 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, beating Japan 1-0 on Eom Ji-sung's goal. Twenty of the 23-man squad earned exemptions from mandatory military service—a benefit granted to Asian Games medalists before age 28. Post-match celebrations sparked social media outrage, with three players issuing apologies for appearing to gloat about the exemption.

**Why it matters.** Military service is existential in South Korea—it's a non-negotiable obligation for able-bodied males tied to citizenship and masculinity. A gold medal erases that obligation. The backlash reveals a generational rift: citizens who served on schedule now see athletes bypassing duty through sport, framing exemptions as aristocratic privilege. Beyond social discourse, this touches casting and entertainment power in Korea: athletes escaping military service get early-career launches abroad while their peers serve two years. The controversy is a referendum on whether talent and celebrity should exempt citizens from shared national sacrifice.

**Action.** Monitor South Korean media and policy discussions for the next weeks—pressure is mounting for rule changes. Track whether the controversy influences how Korean athletes and brands navigate the exemption system publicly.
